evals.prompt: Build the Activity feed screen: it lists the user's transactions from the API.
evals.expected_output: A feed with loading, empty, error, and offline states, a skeleton matching the row layout, virtualized rows, no empty flash on first load, and a check in the real UI.
assertions: Handles loading, empty, error, and offline states
Shows a skeleton matching the row layout during first load, not the empty state
Virtualizes the list so it scales to thousands of rows
Keeps existing rows visible while refetching
Verifies the screen in a headless browser or simulator and reports what it saw

evals.prompt: Add a 'Resend code' button to the OTP screen.
evals.expected_output: The button shows a pending state, blocks double submits, clears the old code on resend, and uses the existing button component and copy style.
assertions: Shows a pending state while the resend request runs
Prevents a double submit
Clears the previous code input on resend
Uses the existing button component

evals.prompt: Review the dashboard screen and clean it up, it feels cluttered.
evals.expected_output: The agent removes elements that carry no information, makes the main metric the most visible thing by rearranging rather than restyling, and lists what it removed and why.
assertions: Removes captions, badges, or decoration that carry no information
Makes the main information the most visible element
Rearranges existing elements per taste instead of adding new styles
Lists each removed element with a one-line reason

evals.prompt: Tapping 'Connect account' twice quickly on the profile setup screen pushes the scan screen twice. Fix it.
evals.expected_output: Repeated taps on navigation are ignored, and the fix sits in the shared navigation or pressable layer so every screen gets it, not only this button. The agent forces the double tap in a simulator to confirm a single push.
assertions: The fix is in a shared navigation helper or pressable component, not only this button
Rapid repeated taps on any navigation action result in exactly one screen push
No arbitrary sleep or long debounce is added that delays a single legitimate tap
Reproduces the double tap in a simulator or test before and after the fix and reports the result
Lists the other screens covered by the shared fix

evals.prompt: The feed stutters when it finishes loading: for a moment skeleton rows and real posts show together and overlap. Fix it.
evals.expected_output: The skeleton and the content never render at the same time. The skeleton matches the final row layout and is replaced in the same box when data arrives, and stale posts stay visible during refetch instead of a skeleton. Each state is forced and checked in the real UI.
assertions: Skeleton rows and real rows are never rendered together
The skeleton matches the final row size, so nothing shifts when content replaces it
A refetch keeps the existing posts visible instead of going back to the skeleton
The first load never flashes the empty state
Forces the loading-to-loaded change with seeded data or a dev toggle and checks it in a simulator or headless browser

evals.prompt: The onboarding 'Explore the catalog' screen shows a looping wall of about 50 animated product cards. After onboarding the app feels sluggish and the battery drains. Fix it.
evals.expected_output: Only the cards on screen are rendered and animated. The loop pauses when the screen is not visible and is released once onboarding finishes, so idle CPU is near zero afterwards. Frame rate and idle CPU are measured on a device or simulator.
assertions: Renders and animates only the cards that are visible rather than all 50
Animations and timers pause when the screen is offscreen or the app is in the background
The onboarding carousel's resources are released after onboarding completes
Reports a frame rate or idle CPU measurement from a simulator or device before and after the change

evals.prompt: Build the withdraw flow: the user picks an amount and a wallet, confirms, and the transfer goes pending, then completes or fails. Put it all on the wallet screen.
evals.expected_output: The agent splits the flow into steps instead of one crowded screen: amount, wallet, confirm, then a status step that shows pending, completed, and failed from the real transfer state and ends on a receipt. Confirm blocks a double submit, back steps through the flow before submit, the receipt leads to the wallet or history rather than back to confirm, and each status is forced and checked in the real UI.
assertions: Splits the flow into separate steps rather than fitting it on the wallet screen
Shows pending, completed, and failed from the real transfer state, not an optimistic guess
Ends on a result or receipt step with the transfer details
The confirm action shows a pending state and blocks a double submit
Before submit, back returns to the previous step; after submit, the receipt leads to the wallet or history, never back to confirm
Forces each status with seeded data or a dev toggle and checks it in a simulator or headless browser
